questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location (high Arctic) and fieldwork included in the courses (since little fieldwork is conducted at my home university).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been a very nice experience, with good accomodation, a great social life and beautiful trips into the nature. But the acamedic aspect was not optimal. The courses were chaotic, and some did not live up to their own course descriptions. We were overburdened with too much compulsary work but the academic level was not high enough. Thus, we were stressed, but our professors did not go in depth with the material, and we did not have enough time to study on our own to compensate for this. They wanted to include too much in too little time and therefore did not go into detail with most of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some time into the first course, I recieved counseling because I was stressed about the work load in combination with a lack of organisation on the course. It is good that UNIS offer counseling.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Upon arrival we received a sheet of paper with the most important information (student e-mail, etc.).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Elvesletta is the one place that UNIS students can and do live.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans. Either you shared a kitchen, or you could rent your own apartment with your own kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: One weird and unacceptable thing about the housing was that you are not allowed to accomodate guests in your own room. This is due to fire safety, they say (so they know how many are in the building). But you can never know how many are in the building, and a way around it could just be to tell the staff that you have visitors. Everyone however ignore this rule, because it is ridiculous, and the hotels in town are really expensive. There is an opportunity to rent a room for guests at the student housing but guest rooms are way too few, and therefore not likely to be available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was new and functioning, had all the facilities you needed. But it was too electrified (heating was controlled at a panel, not a regular radiator knob; you could not control the ventilation in your own room, which was very noisy, and caused me to feel very stressed in my own room). 
When something was out of order, you could quickly had it looked at and fixed.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little confusing having to apply to and be in contact with two institutions, as my Erasmus agreement is with the University of Oslo, and my actual stay was with the University Center in Svalbard (UNIS). But applying of courses at UNIS was easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just go to UNIS' webpage and apply for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't think there is any help in terms of registration, but there are e-mails you can write to for any kind of question regarding your studies at the univeristy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes, I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't have any advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was rushed, not in detail, too much wasteful work (meetings, too many student presentations), too repetetive (they should coordinate between courses, since they prioritise students that take all three courses). But I learned a lot in the fieldwork.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not very high level, but too much work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH is so much more organised and true to their course descriptions. They are way more balanced in the work load and has a more clear objective and theme.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AT-331 Arctic Environmental Pollution: Distribution and Processes, 
AT-330 Arctic Environmental Toxicology, 
AT-324 Techniques for the Detection of Organo-chemical Pollutants in the Arctic Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These three courses are the ones to take for environmental science students in the spring at UNIS.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
It is very cold in March (coldest month) and I had to buy some extra layers for field work. 
Going on guided trips in your free time in Svalbard is very expensive, so it's a good idea to put some money aside for just that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Vegetables were very expensive. 
The canteen is also very expensive, so it is better to prepare your own lunch.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a sportscentre with a gym and swimming pool, there are a few cafés, one small cinema, some museums, and some small music festivals. However, there is not a lot of culture here, so most free time is spent on socialising with your peers.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The housing provided some activities, such as knitting, painting, waffle night. Some student groups volunteered to plan hikes, and there is a cabin that you can be lucky to book (through a lottery). There is also student equipment, that you can apply for for your own private trips. 
There was one dinner in the beginning for people doing the safety course, and some friday gatherings where you could by some canned beers during the semester. Also, there were some extracurriculum lectures at UNIS which was interesting. But no parties at UNIS and the friday "bar" closed very early.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go on a lot of hikes, because the nature is beautiful and the landscape and weather changes so quickly (24h darkness to 24 sunlight in just a few months). 
Fruene is a cosy café where you can get cheaper yarn for knitting every thursday.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again, go on hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is not difficult adjusting to, other than the fact that there isn't a lot of high cultural offers. It is my perception that most locals are families or people living there for natural experiences, so if you like art museums, quality music, cinema, etc., you will miss it here. It is the nature that is interesting here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Every student there is international.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none comes to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the culture for hiking, and enjoying nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare for the courses to be unorganised. 
2. Become a member of Longyearbyen Travel Club - then you can go on boat trips for example for a reduced price.
3. Be aware that the Arctic is a challenging place to live which can be overwhelming at times. With no sunlight in the winter, snowstorms, and a lot of energy spent on keeping warm, you should make sure to get your vitamins and tend to yourself. With polar bears in the wild, extreme weather and avalanche risks, a lot of preparation goes into a hike.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bruktikken is a "store" where you get second hand clothes for free.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences in nature and the social life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the Arctic winter.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
